narrative: The model estimates a 20% probability that you will fail your final year. That is not a certainty, but it is a meaningful risk, and under the rule used to decide support it is enough to place you in remedial courses as a precaution. The strongest warning sign is your reported workday alcohol use: you are in the very high category, while most students who passed report very low workday drinking (84.5%) and only a small minority report low or medium use. This was the top factor pushing the prediction toward failure. The next most influential factor is your record of past class failures: you have none, matching the average of students who passed, so this weighs toward passing. Third is your reason for choosing the school—reputation—which also leans toward passing rather than failure. In other words, two important factors are protective, but the alcohol-use signal is stronger and drives the concern. To improve your position, focus first on reducing workday alcohol use, keep your zero-failure record, maintain steady study habits and attendance, and use family and school support early if work starts to slip. Remedial courses are there to lower the 20% risk before final exams.
